clue.text: Demote soldiers escorting ambassador

indicators.note: one piece escorting another walks beside it, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a stock crossword source of soldiers
a legate is an envoy or papal ambassador

explanation.surface: An ambassador's military escort is being stripped of rank.
explanation.definitionFit: To relegate someone is to move them down to a lower rank or division, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Give up on recruit

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a business letter
to sign a player is to recruit them

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a new recruit, or gives up on them.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase the pieces also say sign again, so the clue hints at two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a post or a game, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Roman official reportedly conquered outer boundaries

indicators.note: reportedly says the word that follows is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: licked, as in beaten, means conquered

indicators.note: the boundaries of a word are its first and last letters, taken here from the word outer

explanation.surface: A Roman official is said to have pushed back the empire's outer frontiers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outer' is not a container signal: its own boundaries, O and R, are the letters wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A lictor was an attendant in ancient Rome who carried the fasces before a magistrate.

clue.text: Irish girl with, say, a Scotsman

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
say introduces an example, abbreviated eg
Ian is a typically Scottish man's name

explanation.surface: An Irish girl turns up accompanied by a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irish' looks as if it describes the girl, but it is the definition on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A Galwegian is someone from Galway, a city in the west of Ireland, so the word is an Irish demonym.

clue.text: Footballers on the move felt strains developing about start of replay

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the next piece
developing means the letters of felt strains are being worked into a new form
start of takes the opening letter of replay

explanation.surface: A footballer feels the strain as a replay begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developing' rearranges FELT STRAINS into TRANSFELIST, and 'about' puts R inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A club's transfer list names the players it is willing to sell, footballers likely to move on.

clue.text: Written test will be in the afternoon presumably? Wrong

definitions.text: Written test will be in the afternoon presumably?
definitions.meaning: if the written paper is after lunch, the spoken exam is in the morning: an a.m. oral
lacking any moral sense, without regard for right and wrong

explanation.surface: An exam timetable puts the written paper after lunch, which someone thinks is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is a cryptic definition: with the written paper in the afternoon, the spoken test is an a.m. oral.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral means without moral standards, unconcerned with whether conduct is right; the setter stretches this to mean wrong.

clue.text: Soil fungus?

definitions.meaning: loose earth rich in rotted matter
a furry growth on damp food or walls

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a growth in the soil is a fungus.
explanation.definitionFit: Mould means both crumbly organic earth and the fuzzy growth that spoils bread, two separate senses.

clue.text: Great star performing in tragedy no end

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters put on a new show, so they are rearranged
no end means the last letter of tragedy is dropped

explanation.surface: A leading actor is starring in a tragedy that never seems to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end' cuts TRAGEDY to TRAGED; 'performing' rearranges IN TRAGED.
explanation.definitionFit: A red giant is a very large, cool, late-stage star, so great here means huge, not famous.

clue.text: What javelin thrower hopes for? He's unlikely to win

definitions.meaning: a javelin thrower wants a throw that travels a great distance
an outsider in a race or contest, at long odds

explanation.surface: A javelin thrower hopes for a big throw, though he is not expected to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A long shot is both a far throw, taken literally, and an outsider with little chance, the idiom.

clue.text: Thus I catch retreating Mafioso?

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed

indicators.note: retreating sends the word for catch backwards

parts.note: to nail a criminal is to catch them

explanation.surface: Someone claims to have caught a mafia man as he backs away.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia began in Sicily, so a Sicilian is offered as a native of the Mafia's island; the question mark flags the stretch.

clue.text: To polish all round study is a responsibility

indicators.note: all round turns the word for polish the other way

parts.note: to rub something is to polish it
a den is a private room for work or study

explanation.surface: Keeping the study polished is a household duty.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden is a heavy load or duty that one must carry, a synonym of responsibility.

clue.text: Outcry as rubbish is dumped in gym and railway terminal

indicators.note: rubbish dumped in something is put inside it

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym
rot means nonsense or rubbish
a station is where trains stop and terminate

explanation.surface: Litter dumped in a gym and a station causes public anger.
explanation.definitionFit: A protestation is a strong declaration of objection, close to an outcry.

clue.text: Good to wander in small wood

parts.note: to rove is to wander about

explanation.surface: It is pleasant to stroll through a little wood.
explanation.definitionFit: A grove is a small group of trees, a little wood.

clue.text: Mum needs cash, we're told, for breakfast cereal

parts.note: mum as in keeping mum means silent, which is the call sh

indicators.note: we're told means the word for cash is heard, not spelt

parts.note: readies is British slang for ready cash

explanation.surface: Mother needs money to buy the breakfast cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mum' looks like a mother but means quiet. Shreddies is a British breakfast cereal of whole-wheat squares.
explanation.definitionFit: Shreddies is a brand of wheat breakfast cereal sold in Britain, an example of the definition.

clue.text: Musical piece: it's recurring in Monteverdi composition

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the rearranged name
composition means the composer's name is put together in a fresh order
recurring here means running back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: the word it, with the 's standing for is, linking

explanation.surface: A musical piece keeps returning to a theme in a Monteverdi work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges MONTEVERDI to DIVERMENTO; 'recurring' makes IT into TI, put 'in' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A divertimento is a light instrumental composition in several movements, popular in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Film technique that's strangely emotive? No

indicators.note: strangely says the letters appear in an odd new order

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a film method is strangely emotional, and the answer is no.
explanation.definitionFit: Movietone was an early sound-on-film system, best known from the Movietone newsreels.

clue.text: Jokes about an east Asian native

indicators.note: about means the jokes go around the next pieces

parts.note: japes are pranks or jokes

explanation.surface: Jokes are told about someone from East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'east Asian' reads as one phrase, but 'east' gives E and only 'Asian native' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A person born in Japan is a native of that Asian country.

clue.text: Going round meadows is utter delight

indicators.note: going round means the word for utter surrounds the meadows

parts.note: pure, as in pure nonsense, means utter or complete
leas are meadows or pasture

explanation.surface: Wandering about the meadows is a complete joy.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is enjoyment or happy satisfaction, a synonym of delight.

clue.text: Kind of holiday tired Indian officer wanted, touring America

parts.note: all in is British slang for exhausted

indicators.note: touring means the officer goes round the country

parts.note: Robert Clive, Clive of India, was the British officer who won India for the East India Company
US is the United States

explanation.surface: An exhausted officer from India wants a package holiday while touring America.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-inclusive holiday has meals, drinks and lodging covered by one price, a type of holiday.

clue.text: One cleric and another keeping company

indicators.note: keeping means one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: another cleric, a dean, heads a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: Two clergymen spend time in each other's company.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is an ordained minister ranked below a priest, one kind of cleric.

clue.text: Position adopted by sacristan ceremoniously

indicators.note: adopted by means the word is taken inside the two clue words that follow, across the gap

explanation.surface: A church sacristan strikes a formal pose during a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a way of standing or a stated view, a synonym of position.

clue.text: A whole continent backing short unpleasant Russian aristocrat

indicators.note: backing means supporting from behind, so the continent comes after
short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: nasty means unpleasant
Asia is a whole continent

explanation.surface: A whole continent turns its back on an unpleasant Russian noblewoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like a reversal signal, but here it simply places ASIA behind NAST.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand Duchess Anastasia was the youngest daughter of Tsar Nicholas II, a Russian royal.

clue.text: Presumably not keen on speed

parts.note: read as wordplay, the entry says the word not written going up, which in a down entry turns it over

explanation.surface: Someone is apparently not fond of driving fast.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: in a down entry, 'up' turns NOT into TON, so TON UP describes the clue word 'not'. Ton-up described 1960s British bikers who rode at 100 mph.
explanation.definitionFit: Ton-up means riding at a hundred miles an hour, as the ton-up boys did, so fond of speed.

clue.text: Earl opening contest

parts.note: a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: A nobleman opens a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like an instruction to take a first letter; it is the synonym VENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is a single competition in a sports programme, a contest.

clue.text: Like horse, one kept by queen, specially trained

indicators.note: kept by means the numeral sits inside the rearranged letters
specially trained says the letters are put through new drills, so rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A horse in the Queen's stables has been specially trained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'specially trained' rearranges QUEEN into EQUNE, and the I is 'kept by' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Equine is the adjective for horses, meaning horselike or relating to horses.

clue.text: Spanish island's Category D prison?

parts.note: Category D is the lowest-security class of British prison, for minor offenders
can is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A Spanish island is home to a low-security jail.
explanation.walkthrough: British prisons run from Category A, top security, down to Category D, open prisons; a D prison holds minor risks.
explanation.definitionFit: Minorcan means belonging to Minorca, a Balearic island of Spain, so it matches the possessive.

clue.text: Old English politician getting tea, say, free of charge

parts.note: ex means former or old
an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: say means the drink is heard as a single letter

parts.note: the drink is pronounced like the letter T

explanation.surface: A retired English MP gets his tea without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Exempt means freed from an obligation such as tax, the sense of free of charge.

clue.text: Prisoner in extremes of trouble has to accept 'bird'

indicators.note: has to accept means the outer letters take in the bird
extremes of takes the first and last letters of trouble

parts.note: the erne is a sea eagle, a crossword stalwart

explanation.surface: A jailed man in trouble has to accept doing time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bird' in quotation marks hints at the British slang for prison time, but here it is a real bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is someone confined, usually in wartime, without trial, a type of prisoner.
